update_log: Exhaustive expansion including Ancient, Medieval, British-era (Anglo wars), and Post-Independence (India-Pak, India-China) wars for complete History Static GK.

ancient_battles.fought_between: King Sudas (Bharata tribe) and a confederacy of Ten Kings
ancient_battles.significance_and_outcome: Mentioned in the Rigveda (Mandala 7). King Sudas emerged victorious on the banks of the Ravi (Parushni) river.

ancient_battles.fought_between: Alexander the Great and King Porus
ancient_battles.significance_and_outcome: Fought on the banks of the Jhelum river. Alexander won, but was so impressed by Porus that he reinstated him as a satrap.

ancient_battles.fought_between: Chandragupta Maurya and Seleucus I Nicator
ancient_battles.significance_and_outcome: Chandragupta Maurya won, securing the Indus Valley and parts of modern-day Afghanistan, cemented by a matrimonial alliance.

ancient_battles.fought_between: Mauryan Empire (Ashoka) and State of Kalinga
ancient_battles.significance_and_outcome: Ashoka won but the massive bloodshed led him to embrace Buddhism and a policy of non-violence (Dhamma).

medieval_battles.significance_and_outcome: Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori, who barely escaped with his life.
Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan, laying the foundation for Muslim rule in Northern India.

medieval_battles.fought_between: Muhammad Ghori and Jaichand of Kannauj
medieval_battles.significance_and_outcome: Ghori defeated and killed Jaichand, severely weakening Rajput power in the region.
Babur defeated Lodi using artillery and the Tulughma formation, marking the end of the Delhi Sultanate and beginning of the Mughal Empire.

medieval_battles.fought_between: Babur and Rana Sanga of Mewar
medieval_battles.significance_and_outcome: Babur won, firmly establishing Mughal supremacy in northern India over the Rajput confederacy.
Babur captured the fortress of Chanderi, further weakening Rajput resistance.
Babur defeated the allied Afghan and Bengal forces. This was his last major battle.
Sher Shah Suri defeated Mughal Emperor Humayun, establishing his dominance.
Sher Shah completely routed Humayun, forcing him into exile and establishing the Sur Empire.

medieval_battles.fought_between: Akbar (led by Bairam Khan) and Hemu (Hemchandra Vikramaditya)
medieval_battles.significance_and_outcome: Akbar won after Hemu was struck in the eye by an arrow, re-establishing the Mughal Empire.
The combined forces of the Deccan Sultanates defeated Rama Raya, leading to the complete destruction of the Vijayanagara Empire.

medieval_battles.fought_between: Mughal Empire (led by Raja Man Singh) and Maharana Pratap of Mewar
medieval_battles.significance_and_outcome: Mughal victory on the field, but Maharana Pratap escaped and continued guerrilla warfare against the Mughals.
A decisive battle in the Mughal war of succession. Aurangzeb won, leading to his capture of the Mughal throne.

modern_battles_and_british_era.fought_between: Nader Shah of Persia and Mughal Emperor Muhammad Shah
modern_battles_and_british_era.significance_and_outcome: Nader Shah crushed the Mughal army, sacked Delhi, and looted the Peacock Throne and Koh-i-Noor diamond.

modern_battles_and_british_era.fought_between: Kingdom of Travancore (Marthanda Varma) and the Dutch East India Company
modern_battles_and_british_era.significance_and_outcome: Travancore decisively defeated the Dutch, effectively ending Dutch colonial ambitions in India.

modern_battles_and_british_era.fought_between: British East India Company (Robert Clive) and Siraj-ud-Daulah
modern_battles_and_british_era.significance_and_outcome: Clive won through the betrayal of Mir Jafar. It marked the beginning of British political hegemony in Bengal.

modern_battles_and_british_era.fought_between: British EIC (Sir Eyre Coote) and French EIC (Comte de Lally)
modern_battles_and_british_era.significance_and_outcome: A decisive British victory in the Third Carnatic War, ending French political ambitions in India.

modern_battles_and_british_era.fought_between: Maratha Empire and Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani Empire)
modern_battles_and_british_era.significance_and_outcome: Abdali decisively defeated the Marathas, checking Maratha expansion and creating a power vacuum for the British.

modern_battles_and_british_era.fought_between: British EIC (Hector Munro) vs. Combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula, and Shah Alam II
modern_battles_and_british_era.significance_and_outcome: Decisive British victory leading to the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), granting the EIC Diwani rights (tax collection) over Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.

modern_battles_and_british_era.fought_between: British EIC and Hyder Ali of Mysore
modern_battles_and_british_era.significance_and_outcome: Hyder Ali defeated the British, forcing them to sign the Treaty of Madras.

modern_battles_and_british_era.battle_name: Second Anglo-Mysore War (Battle of Porto Novo)
modern_battles_and_british_era.fought_between: British EIC (Sir Eyre Coote) and Hyder Ali / Tipu Sultan
modern_battles_and_british_era.significance_and_outcome: Hyder Ali died during the war. Tipu Sultan continued it, ending in a stalemate and the Treaty of Mangalore.

modern_battles_and_british_era.fought_between: British EIC (Lord Cornwallis) and Tipu Sultan
modern_battles_and_british_era.significance_and_outcome: Tipu Sultan was defeated and forced to sign the humiliating Treaty of Seringapatam, giving up half his territory.

modern_battles_and_british_era.fought_between: British EIC (Lord Wellesley) and Tipu Sultan
modern_battles_and_british_era.significance_and_outcome: Decisive British victory. Tipu Sultan was killed defending his capital, Srirangapatna.

modern_battles_and_british_era.fought_between: British EIC (Arthur Wellesley) and Maratha Empire (Scindia and Bhonsle)
modern_battles_and_british_era.significance_and_outcome: A major battle of the Second Anglo-Maratha War. British won a hard-fought victory, breaking Maratha power in the Deccan.
British victory resulting in the Treaty of Lahore. The Sikh Empire had to cede the Jullundur Doab and Kashmir.
Decisive British victory at Gujrat (the 'Battle of Guns') led to the complete annexation of Punjab by Lord Dalhousie.

post_independence_wars.significance_and_outcome: Triggered by tribal militias crossing into Kashmir. Ended with a UN-mediated ceasefire and the establishment of the Ceasefire Line (now Line of Control). Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession.
Fought over border disputes in Aksai Chin and NEFA (Arunachal Pradesh). Ended when China declared a unilateral ceasefire, retaining de facto control of Aksai Chin.
Triggered by Pakistan's 'Operation Gibraltar'. Ended in a UN-mandated ceasefire and the signing of the Tashkent Declaration by Lal Bahadur Shastri.

post_independence_wars.fought_between: India (along with Mukti Bahini) and Pakistan
post_independence_wars.significance_and_outcome: Decisive Indian victory leading to the surrender of 93,000 Pakistani troops. Resulted in the creation of Bangladesh and the signing of the Shimla Agreement (1972).

Triggered by Pakistani infiltration across the LoC into Kargil. India launched 'Operation Vijay' to recapture the heights. Ended with complete Indian victory (celebrated as Kargil Vijay Diwas on July 26).
